pick.headline: European Community recognizes Croatia and Slovenia
pick.summary: On January 15, 1992, the European Community member states recognized Croatia and Slovenia as independent states.
pick.significance: Recognition, pressed by Germany, marked the international end of Yugoslavia and turned attention to Bosnia.
pick.fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of January 15, 1992, carried Bulgarian Foreign Minister Ganev, via FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE, urging that Macedonia be recognized alongside Slovenia and Croatia on January 15, warning that refusing it would encourage Serbian annexation.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: East Europe, No. 010, 15 January 1992
evidence.snippet: FBIS-EEU-92-010 15 January 1992 the abovementioned EC declaration, and should be treated on an equal footing with Slovenia and Croatia. Bulgarian is convinced that any postponement of the international recognition that the Republic of Mace- donia should receive will do little to promote stability in the Balkans. alternates.headline: Crowds storm Stasi headquarters in East Berlin
alternates.summary: On January 15, 1990, demonstrators broke into the East German Ministry for State Security headquarters on Normannenstrasse in East Berlin.
alternates.significance: The storming came amid fears that the Stasi was destroying its files. The archive that survived later let millions of East Germans read what had been gathered on them.
